description:
SecuredMe (Quebec) — Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

* Mission: A multi-scale Mars terrain map where a rover scouts the ground before astronauts walk it: slope, roughness and hazards from HiRISE & MOLA elevation data.

* Engine: Python (rasterio, NumPy), fractal multi-scale analysis, neutrosophic ⟨T,I,F⟩ confidence per map cell.

* Front: interactive web map.

* Standard: open NASA data, pytest-verified, reproducible.

* Looking for: GIS / planetary science, UX / 3D.
summary: Most Mars maps treat an orbital terrain model as ground truth, but the hazards that break a rover wheel or exhaust an astronaut live in the scale gap between coarse orbital pixels (64 m) and the 1–4 m footprint of a person on the ground. MarsWalk is an EVA survival map for Jezero Crater that confronts multi-scale slopes (1, 4, 16 and 64 m) derived from the USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE 1 m DTM with 708 real waypoints and measured tilts from NASA's Perseverance rover. Where scales disagree, MarsWalk shows it: at the Sol 700 scarp the 64 m map reads 11.2° (caution) while the 4 m slope is 22.1° (no-go) and Perseverance measured 20.5°. Every cell carries a GO / CAUTION / NO_GO verdict with a confidence score, every number is tagged MEASURED, DERIVED or SIMULATED and sealed with SHA-256, and an obstacle-aware planner routes astronauts around scarps within xEVA slope, walk-back, oxygen, radiation and radio limits. It never says GO on missing data.
details:
1. WHAT MARSWALK DOES & THE CORE DISCOVERY

Most planetary mapping portals treat coarse orbital Digital Terrain Models (DTMs) as ground truth. On Mars, however, the hazards that break a rover wheel or exhaust a suited astronaut live in the scale gap between orbital pixels (64 m regional grids) and a 1–4 m human footprint.

MarsWalk is an Extravehicular Activity (EVA) survival map and obstacle-aware route planner for Jezero Crater and the Western Delta Fan (18.38° N, 77.58° E). By confronting multi-scale slopes (1 m, 4 m, 16 m, and 64 m Horn 3x3 baselines from the USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE 1 m/px DTM) against 708 real Perseverance waypoints and measured rover tilts (Sol 13 to Sol 2022), MarsWalk exposes systematic orbital smoothing:

• Systematic Scale Bias: Coarse 64 m orbital grids underestimate steep delta scarps (>10°) by -5.05° on average, hiding >20° suit-limit walls.

• The Sol 700 Scarp Trap: At Sol 700, the 64 m orbital map reads 11.2° (CAUTION), whereas MarsWalk's 4 m kernel detects 22.1° (NO_GO Veto)—confirmed by Perseverance's measured 20.5° ground tilt.

• Ground-Truth Validation: Achieves 97.7% specificity (43/44 traversable stops) on a disjoint odd/even Sol validation split.

2. HOW IT WORKS: PLITHOGENIC MULTI-SCALE ENGINE & SAFETY VETOES

Instead of collapsing terrain risk into a single opaque score, MarsWalk evaluates every cell as a Plithogenic Neutrosophic triplet <T, I, F> (Truth / Indeterminacy / Falsity) across 10 normalized terrain carriers (slope, roughness, scale divergence, curvature, Hurst exponent, rock CFA, sky-view factor, solar shadow, walk-back distance, and Area of Applicability):

• Persistent-Hazard Override: If fine neighboring scales (4 m and 16 m) flag a steep scarp while the 64 m baseline smooths it out, the engine forbids pruning the fine-scale hazard.

• Non-Compensatory Lexicographic Safety Vetoes: High science value never overrides crew survival. Any 4 m slope > 20.0° (NASA xEVA suit limit), walk-back > 2,000 m, missing/out-of-bounds data, or active Solar Particle Event triggers an immediate NO_GO veto.

• Cryptographic Epistemic Honesty: Every metric carries a mandatory MEASURED, DERIVED, or SIMULATED provenance tag sealed with SHA-256 in manifest.json. Unavailable layers in this window are explicitly declared out-of-pack (0% fabricated data).

3. HUMAN EVA FACTORS CONSIDERED

• Obstacle-Aware Routing (M1/M2): Clusters >= 4 m x 4 m rock/scarp hazards at 1 m/px, dilates obstacles by 0.85 m (0.55 m xEVA suit half-width + 0.30 m TRN 1-sigma uncertainty), and routes crews via 16-neighbor anisotropic A* (e.g., safely routing around the Sol 700 scarp via Sol 413 -> Sol 609 -> Sol 753 with max slope 13.3° <= 20.0° and walk-back <= 2,000 m).

• Suited Metabolism & O2 Budget (M4): Models Martian 0.3794 g suited locomotion (121 kg MKIII/xEVA class) using Minetti (2002) and Pandolf-CSRM equations.

• Radiation & Topographic Occlusion (M3): Uses Curiosity RAD GCR baseline (0.64 mSv/day) with analytical scarp-toe sky-view occlusion (7.0%–9.1% GCR reduction, without false SPE shelter claims).

• UHF 414.2 MHz Comms Shadowing (M6): Computes 1st Fresnel zone clearance and Bullington knife-edge diffraction (ITU-R P.526) between a 3.0 m rover mast and 1.8 m astronaut antenna over the Mars sphere.

4. CREATIVITY, BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

MarsWalk shifts planetary cartography from "pretty orbital visualization" to fail-safe operational verification. It delivers dual mission formats from the same < 5 MB SHA-256-sealed data pack:

1) An interactive 2D/3D web tactical HUD (EN/FR/ES, accessibility modes, rover Navcam ground-truth inspection, and live route assessment).

2) A deterministic standalone vector SVG xEVA Survival Map Card for offline mission binders, habitat screens, and wrist tablets.

5. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE

• Languages & Backend: Python, FastAPI, NumPy/SciPy geospatial pipelines, Hypothesis, SALib Sobol sensitivity analysis, Pytest, Ruff.

• Frontend & 3D Visualization: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, MapLibre GL, Three.js, Vitest, WebMCP instrumentation.

• Integrated Datasets: USGS HiRISE 1 m DTM (blended with MOLA), NASA Trek HiRISE 25 cm WMTS, Mars 2020 MMGIS 708 Waypoints & 45.2 km Traverse, Mars 2020 Raw Navcam/Mastcam-Z imagery, USGS SIM 3464 Geologic Map, and peer-reviewed NASA xEVA / JPL / Curiosity RAD constraints.

6. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE & PROJECT LINKS

Engineered under human architectural and scientific authority by Jean-Sébastien Beaulieu (Engine, Plithogenic Math, Geodesy & Middleware) and Philippe Pierre (Frontend Cartography, 3D Terrain & UX). SI coding assistants (Claude Code, Google Gemini / Antigravity, OpenAI Codex) were used for code generation, debugging, documentation editing, and hostile verification audits; all physical equations, thresholds, NASA/USGS data bindings, and automated test suites (Pytest + Vitest) were human-defined and deterministically verified.

• Live Interactive App: https://marswalk.securedme.ca/

• Open-Source Repository & SHA-256 Data Pack (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/SeCuReDmE-main-dev/marswalk
